reference: Runnable cases use GNU Bash type/help builtin behavior plus the documented ipcctl API and loadable synopsis in docs/sol-ipcctl.md and config/bash-loadables.list. GNU ipcrm is related but does not accept ipcctl's interface, and its removal operations cannot be run safely here. No operation behavior is claimed as parity.
coverage: Bash identifies ipcctl as a builtin while the candidate fixture has an empty PATH.
Short-help output matches the configured ipcctl short description.
Full help metadata presents the configured description and the documented command synopsis, ID grammar, and removal policy.
Deferred operation coverage is specified separately for shared memory, message queues, and semaphore sets.
exclusions: No System V IPC removal command is executed. Future operation validation requires a disposable Linux VM with a private IPC namespace and objects allocated by the fixture, or a closed syscall mock that cannot call the kernel.
No GNU parity claim is made for ipcrm because its CLI is not a direct match for ipcctl.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves ipcctl as a builtin; the candidate fixture uses an empty PATH, so this verifies its loadable registration without invoking the operation.
Check Bash's short-help metadata against ipcctl's configured short description in bash-loadables.list.
cases.stdout: ipcctl: Run gated System V IPC control operations

cases.purpose: Check that builtin help contains the documented ipcctl synopsis, decimal ID constraint, and exact opt-in policy; the fixture emits a fixed marker after all fields are found.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ipcctl)
[[ $doc == *'ipcctl --rm shm|msg|sem <id>'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'IDs must contain only decimal digits and fit in a nonnegative int.'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'Mutating removal requires BASHOS_IPCRM_ALLOW_RMID=1.'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'documented ipcctl help fields present\n'

cases.purpose: Validate gated shared-memory removal, policy denial, and exact-object selection.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with a private IPC namespace and working System V shared memory. A future fixture must allocate two IPC_PRIVATE mode-0600 segments itself, use only those returned IDs, verify that an unset/non-1 policy preserves both, verify that exact policy value 1 removes only the selected segment via an independent IPC_STAT check, and clean up only IDs it allocated. A closed shmctl mock that cannot reach the kernel is an acceptable alternative for validating IPC_RMID dispatch and the null argument.
